newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden could postpone EMU link until 2003 - report.
newsitem.headline: Sweden could postpone EMU link until 2003 - report.

text.p: Sweden's Prime Minister Goran Persson and Finance Minister Erik Asbrink do not want the country to join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) during the next mandate period 1998-2002 without new parliamentary elections being held, the Swedish radio news Ekot reported on Wednesday.

"According to Ekot's sources, Goran Persson and Erik Asbrink agree that the (ruling) Social Democrats cannot say no to EMU now and then join during the next mandate period without new parliamentary elections being held," the public radio said.
"This means that there will either be new elections or that Sweden cannot be a member of EMU until 2003 after scheduled parliamentary elections in 2002 -- if Persson and Asbrink get to decide."
The Social Democratic top is expected to announce its EMU view on Friday, the radio said.
